title: E1 Stage-Orthogonal Causal Emergence / E-CERT2
candidate: E-CERT2 Dual-Axis Stage-Orthogonal Causal Emergence Certificate
summary: Emergence measurement is split into multiscale intervention-grounded causal contribution and persistent role-identifiable organization. Strong emergent-organ candidacy requires both axes plus causal-basis, selection, projection/uptake, confounder, partition-search, robustness and independent-evaluation gates.
durable_findings: Behavioral endpoint rescue can succeed while the causal mechanism/future re-entry remains broken.
Role-insensitive member overlap can create false recurrence when causal roles are permuted.
Bivariate transfer entropy can be dominated by a common driver and should not be treated as direct causality without conditioning/intervention.
Post-hoc macro/assembly partition search can inflate emergence-looking information scores under a true null; held-out/search-null validation is required.
Bundled graph/workspace/projection/re-entry contrasts can be large under additive nulls; stage-orthogonal factorial attribution is required.
A single scalar causal-emergence/Phi/PID/PEID value is insufficient as an emergent-organ certificate; architecture/scale/estimator dependence must be profiled.
Functional emergent-organ candidacy and phenomenal consciousness remain separate questions.

external_evidence.role: aggregate causal-emergence scalar can be architecture-dominated

external_evidence.ref: ICLR 2026 Emergent Coordination in Multi-Agent Language Models
external_evidence.role: temporal synergy distinguished from performance-relevant coordinated complementarity via interventions/nulls
coarse-graining dependence and alternative dynamical-reversibility shadow
micro-to-macro causal discovery and counterfactual probing in LLM-agent simulations
